addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. - frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). title:	backend: add section-scoped grants behind one visibility resolver
state:	OPEN
author:	maxi-smidt (Maximilian Smidt)
labels:	enhancement
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	Family Tree (Backlog)
milestone:	v2
issue-type:	
parent:	maxi-smidt/family-tree#980
sub-issues:	
sub-issues-completed:	
blocked-by:	maxi-smidt/family-tree#993
blocking:	maxi-smidt/family-tree#1024, maxi-smidt/family-tree#1017, maxi-smidt/family-tree#990, maxi-smidt/family-tree#987, maxi-smidt/family-tree#986, maxi-smidt/family-tree#985, maxi-smidt/family-tree#983
number:	984
--
Part of #980. Depends on #982 and the lossless grant model in #993.

- Enforce whole-workspace and section-scoped user, invitation, and public-access grants through one visible-member/content resolver in the authorization deps — never through route-specific ad hoc filters.
- Scoped grants see only members assigned to their sections. Relations crossing out of scope render as protected placeholders with no names, counts, ids usable for probing, or other metadata leakage.
- Resolve overlapping grants deterministically using #993's per-scope roles and domain restrictions; do not flatten several scopes into one over-permissive membership.
- Apply #993's explicit provenance/visibility rule to content without member links as well as content linked to visible members.
- Identity-link targets and continuation counts outside the caller's scope are protected placeholders and disclose no workspace/member metadata.
- Cache keys, search, statistics, activity, export, SSE/presence, media authorization, and every eager store load use the same resolved visibility boundary.

Minimal product scope remains only what the v2 migration requires; richer owner-facing section-sharing UX is a follow-up.

Acceptance criteria:

- The before/after access matrix for every migrated user/public principal is identical for members and all content domains.
- A user with different roles or restrictions in overlapping sections receives the correct effective permission for each record and action.
- Direct-id, search, graph, count/statistics, export, media, activity, and realtime paths cannot reveal an out-of-scope record.
- Cross-boundary relations and identity links return stable protected placeholders without sensitive metadata.
- Authorization tests exercise whole-workspace grants, overlapping scoped grants, invitations, public passwords, unlinked content, admins, and revoked access.

Feature flag: none. Migration-required authorization is core workspace behavior.


## Read/write action matrix

The resolver returns one WorkspaceAccessContext used for reads and mutations. Evaluate each applicable grant as a unit; never combine the editor role from one scope with the unrestricted domains of another.

- Scalar member edit requires an applicable editor grant; the UI/API reports that a canonical boundary record changes in every readable section.
- Relation create/update requires write permission for both endpoints. Delete/merge requires owner permission or editor permission across every affected member scope and content record.
- Section membership, grants, invitations, public links, and content re-scoping are owner/admin actions unless an explicit narrower capability is introduced.
- Content decisions use durable provenance from #1023, including zero-link and mixed-link records.
- Out-of-scope direct ids have the same 404 shape/timing policy as nonexistent ids. Placeholder identifiers are access-version-scoped pseudonyms, not reusable global member ids.
- Search, graph cursors, counts/statistics, export, media, activity, caches, SSE audiences/payloads, and presence rosters/editing ids use the same visibility fingerprint and invalidate immediately on policy changes.
- Access-equivalence tests compare permitted actions as well as readable rows and cover revoke/role/restriction races.

title:	sharing: preserve legacy access across workspace consolidation
state:	OPEN
author:	maxi-smidt (Maximilian Smidt)
labels:	enhancement
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	Family Tree (Backlog)
milestone:	v2
issue-type:	
parent:	maxi-smidt/family-tree#980
sub-issues:	
sub-issues-completed:	
blocked-by:	maxi-smidt/family-tree#1023
blocking:	maxi-smidt/family-tree#1017, maxi-smidt/family-tree#997, maxi-smidt/family-tree#984
number:	993
--
Part of #980. Depends on durable content provenance in #1023 and must be settled before #984 and #987.

The v1 source model can contain several grants for the same collaborator after
same-owner trees consolidate: different roles, domain restrictions, and public
passwords on different constituent trees. A single
`workspace_memberships.section_scope` list and one workspace-level public-link
configuration cannot represent those states without widening or narrowing
access.

Design and implement the normalized v2 grant model used by migration and the
visibility resolver:

- Preserve role and domain restrictions independently for each migrated
  section scope. A user may therefore be editor in one section and viewer or
  differently restricted in another.
- Preserve every active public link, including its password, access version,
  role, and section scope. Do not merge several legacy public links into one
  more-permissive link.
- Carry section scope through outstanding invitations and accepted invitation
  flows.
- Use #1023's durable origin scope for every content record—including linked, mixed-linked, and unlinked content—so migrated users retain exactly the records and actions they had before consolidation.
- Define deterministic effective-role/restriction resolution when scopes
  overlap, including whole-workspace grants.
- Keep new shares unscoped by default; richer owner-facing section-sharing UX
  remains out of scope beyond what migration and current sharing flows need.

Acceptance criteria:

- A fixture where one user has different roles/restrictions on two trees can
  consolidate without access widening or loss.
- Multiple public links with different passwords remain independently usable
  and section-scoped after migration.
- Pending invitations retain their original scope when accepted after
  migration.
- Unlinked content from one constituent tree never leaks to a collaborator of
  another constituent tree and remains visible to its original collaborators.
- Database constraints reject cross-workspace section references and invalid
  overlapping/whole-workspace grant states.

Feature flag: none. This is required migration and authorization infrastructure
for the hard v2 cutover.


## Grant-composition and public-link hardening

number:	982
--
Part of #980. Depends on #981.

- New tables: `sections`, `section_members` (explicit assignment; overlap allowed; membership optional), `section_positions` (per-section layout overlay, replacing `Member.position_x/y` as the layout home).
- CRUD routes for sections; creating a section seeds membership from a traversal preview reusing `services/trees/subtree_selection.py`. Preview reports primary members, boundary people, connections to existing sections, and counts.
- Creating/deleting a section never copies, moves, or deletes people, relationships, media, or documents.
- New-member section suggestions (from parents/partner) that require user confirmation.

## Hardening requirements

- Define fresh/imported-workspace default-section behavior, normalized name/order constraints, indexes in both membership directions, and database-level same-workspace constraints for sections, members, and layout nodes.
- Specify shared section overlays versus per-user viewport/camera/collapse state; layout state must not leak between users or remain on Member rows.
- Section preview returns a revision-bound token. Creation revalidates changed members/relations instead of applying a stale traversal silently.
- Membership mutation is access-sensitive: a scoped editor may operate only inside their already-visible set and can never add an arbitrary hidden member to expand their own scope. Changes that alter grants/public audiences require owner authorization.
- Section deletion previews dependent grants, public links, invitations, saved views, positions, and provenance. Use RESTRICT plus explicit reassignment/removal; never cascade a scope into workspace-wide access. Genealogy/content remains untouched.
- New-member suggestions and confirmed assignments commit atomically with member creation or leave a deterministic unassigned result.
- Record activity/audit entries and invalidate visibility/cache/cursor versions after membership changes.
